open_points.subject: functions.add_trial_case file fixtures
open_points.text: Inputs: A contract version, input values by port, optional expected outputs, the actor.
open_points.question: How are the bytes of authored file inputs and expected file outputs supplied to add_trial_case, rather than only their digest, size and media-type facts?
options: Supply file bytes directly with each file-port value
Supply a previously published byte object or upload reference
Accept only file facts and require another operation to publish the bytes
open_points.default_guess: Supply file bytes directly with each file-port value and let functions publish them through store.put_value_bytes.

open_points.subject: authored trial-case port coverage
open_points.text: input values by port, optional expected outputs
open_points.question: Must an authored case contain exactly every contract input, reject extra input names, and, when expected_outputs is present, contain exactly every contract output rather than a subset?
options: Require the exact input set and either no expected_outputs or the exact output set
Require exact inputs but allow expected outputs for only selected ports
Require named values to fit and ignore extra names
open_points.default_guess: Require the exact input set and either no expected_outputs or the exact output set.

open_points.subject: trial execution value-size handling
open_points.text: sandbox.execute_function says “stored_value_bytes_max and the spool ceilings are not the sandbox's — runs and store apply them after the execution has otherwise succeeded”, while M07 permits detail_code value_too_large and functions records trial value outputs as StoredValues.
open_points.question: What happens when a trial or admission execution returns a schema-valid value within output_bytes but above stored_value_bytes_max?
options: Record contract_violation with detail_code value_too_large
Record a successful trial and store the oversized value
Return internal_error because the output cannot be persisted
open_points.default_guess: Record contract_violation with detail_code value_too_large before attempting to persist the value.

open_points.subject: bindings.check_installed_instances manifest validation
open_points.text: an unreadable record, or one failing a check of the record itself (A08 rule 5), fails at its service
open_points.question: Which A08 rule 5 checks are performed at startup when check_installed_instances has no operation name or proposed ports, and in what order are multiple capabilities examined?
options: Check only the service-record envelope and the selected instance facts needed for header collision
Validate every capability entry, in a specified capability order
Apply only checks independent of any operation or proposal and defer all capability checks
open_points.default_guess: Check only the service-record envelope and selected instance facts needed to detect required-header collisions.

open_points.subject: SpooledFile identity
open_points.text: M22 says “equal facts are the same spooled file”, but State 5 says “A SpooledFile is named by its producing position alone (SpooledFileKey)” and read_spooled_file omits digest, size and media type.
open_points.question: Is a SpooledFile's identity all of its M22 facts or only (run_id, producer_node_id, map_index, attempt_number, producer_port, list_index)?
options: Producing-position key only; digest, size, media type and class are attributes
All M22 facts, so callers must supply them to identify the record
A separate positional lookup key and a distinct content-derived SpooledFile identity
open_points.default_guess: Use the producing-position tuple as the sole record identity and treat the remaining facts as immutable attributes.

open_points.subject: runs.resume_run and continuation operations
open_points.text: resume_run, continue_after_approval and continue_after_resolution all advance the run, but their Errors sections omit stop_required even though the conventions say unconfirmed sandbox cleanup returns stop_required up the call chain.
open_points.question: Can each of these operations return stop_required when later advancement executes a function whose cleanup cannot be confirmed?
options: Yes, all advancing operations propagate stop_required
Only start_run and startup recovery can return stop_required
Convert stop_required to internal_error inside runs
open_points.default_guess: All operations that advance a run propagate stop_required to surface, which answers internal_error and terminates the process.

open_points.subject: runs.continue_after_approval observable effect
open_points.text: “An approved effect is sent in this request” conflicts with the rule that the element reruns pre-send checks and may conclude operation_failed while leaving the approval unused.
open_points.question: Is sending guaranteed after approval, or may the request finish without a send when a repeated pre-send check fails or the rebuilt request requires different authority?
options: Sending is conditional on the repeated pre-send and authority checks
Approval bypasses pre-send checks and guarantees a send
A failed repeated check makes the approval operation itself refuse
open_points.default_guess: Sending is conditional; the approval decision is recorded, but a pre-send failure can conclude the element without sending.

open_points.subject: flow edge guards
open_points.text: “the guard port is a one output of the edge's source node ... its schema is a closed set” does not require value carriage, although runtime equality is defined against a declared closed value.
open_points.question: May a file output port be used as a guard port, and if so how are file bytes compared with the guard value?
options: Only value-carriage output ports may be guards
File ports may be guards by comparing their content digest
File ports may be guards by comparing raw bytes with an encoded guard value
open_points.default_guess: Reject a guard unless its port has value carriage.

open_points.subject: ordering of embedded output collections
open_points.text: “Every collection in an output is in store order unless the operation names another order.” Ports, nodes, edges, constants and other embedded value collections have no store positions.
open_points.question: In what order must read_contract_version, read_binding and read_flow_version return embedded order-free collections?
options: Use the canonical sorting orders of A01
Preserve the order of the first accepted submission
Leave embedded collection order unspecified while ordering only record collections
open_points.default_guess: Return embedded order-free collections in the canonical A01 sorting order.

open_points.subject: store order within one transaction
open_points.text: “The records exist, all of them or none” and “store adds ... store positions” do not define the relative positions of several new records written by one named change, except for NodeExecutions explicitly ordered elsewhere.
open_points.question: How are store positions assigned within changes that create several records, such as a verdict plus activation, a run plus input StoredValues, or a trial case plus StoredValues?
options: Use the order in the Named store changes writes column, with plural records in a fixed identifier order
Give the owning record the first position and auxiliary values later
Treat all records in one transaction as sharing a position with a deterministic subposition
open_points.default_guess: Assign distinct consecutive positions in the listed write order, sorting plural records by their canonical identifiers.

open_points.subject: service api_base_url
open_points.text: An api_base_url is accepted when it is “an absolute http or https URL with a host”, while invocation uses “the api_base_url without a trailing / followed by the declared path”.
open_points.question: Are base URLs containing a path, query, fragment, user information, or multiple trailing slashes valid, and exactly how are they joined to the operation path?
options: Permit only scheme, authority and an optional single trailing slash
Permit a base path but forbid query, fragment and user information, joining path segments by a fixed rule
Accept every absolute URL with a host and concatenate text exactly as stated
open_points.default_guess: Permit scheme and authority with an optional base path, forbid query, fragment and user information, and join with exactly one slash.

open_points.subject: plain HTTP loopback exception
open_points.text: “one whose api_base_url host is a loopback address”
open_points.question: Does the loopback exception apply only to a literal loopback IP address in the URL, or also to hostnames such as localhost or names that currently resolve to loopback?
options: Only literal IPv4 or IPv6 loopback addresses
The hostname localhost plus literal loopback addresses
Any hostname whose DNS result is entirely loopback at connection time
open_points.default_guess: Allow only literal IPv4 or IPv6 loopback addresses.
